answer: Under pairwise rendezvous memory bonds, every identity on the knoll network must meet each partner at a scheduled rendezvous where both parties jointly derive a shared secret unique to that pair, hashing it into a one-time proof that anchors a permanent thread in the ledger. An attacker running n fake identities on the island must generate and store n(n−1)/2 distinct secrets and proofs, so 1,000 fakes demand roughly 499,500 bonds while 100 honest agents each need only 99, keeping verification cheap for real users and prohibitively quadratic for sybil farms.
